candidates.change_summary: Change stored block to block.number instead of block.number + 1
Remove the require check that msg.value equals 1 ether
Delete the statement that sets guesses[msg.sender].block = block.number + 1
Delete the statement that sets guesses[msg.sender].guess = hash
Delete the require that guesses[msg.sender].block == 0, allowing overwrite
Insert require(false) at the beginning to always revert
Removed the requirement that guesses[msg.sender].block equals 0 in lockInGuess.
Changed the required payment in lockInGuess from 1 ether to 2 ether.
Changed the recorded guess target block from block.number + 1 to block.number.
Deleted the statement that records the caller's guessed hash in guesses[msg.sender].guess.
Replace blockhash(guesses[msg.sender].block) with blockhash(block.number) so answer is always zero, changing settle outcome for any guess.
Replace guesses[msg.sender].guess == answer with guesses[msg.sender].guess != answer, inverting who wins.
Delete guesses[msg.sender].block = 0 so settle can be called multiple times by the same sender.
Replace block.number > guesses[msg.sender].block with block.number >= guesses[msg.sender].block, allowing settle in the exact block the guess locks, changing the blockhash used.
Change transfer amount from 2 ether to 1 ether, changing the ETH balance change observed by the caller.
Change transfer amount from 2 ether to 3 ether, causing settle to revert due to insufficient contract balance when a correct guess is made.
Delete require(address(this).balance >= 2 ether) so settle can transfer even if balance is insufficient (revert on transfer instead of require).
Weaken the first settle guard so any sender with a nonzero lock block can proceed, regardless of whether the current block is past it.
Replace the lock check with a tautology so settle can be called even for addresses that never locked a guess.
Replace the answer computation with an unrelated hash so a correct guess no longer pays out.
Change the answer to always be zero so only a guess of bytes32(0) succeeds.
Remove the state reset before payout so the caller's lock remains set after settle.
Change the winning-payout condition from equality to inequality so incorrect guesses trigger the payout branch.
Lower the payout balance requirement to 1 ether so payout can proceed in more states.
Change the payout amount from 2 ether to 1 ether so a winning settle transfers a different value.
Change the required guess lock-out check from block == 0 to block != 0, making already-locked guesses usable and fresh guesses rejected.
Change the settlement timing check from block.number > guesses[msg.sender].block to block.number >= guesses[msg.sender].block, allowing settlement one block earlier.
Change the answer hash input from blockhash(guesses[msg.sender].block) to blockhash(block.number), making the answer depend on the current block instead of the guessed block.
Change the answer hash algorithm from keccak256 to sha256, altering the expected winning guess value.
Change the winning-guess comparison from equality to inequality, so settlement pays out on a wrong guess and reverts on the correct one.
Change the payout balance guard from requiring 2 ether to requiring 1 ether, allowing settlement to complete with less contract balance.
Change the payout amount from 2 ether to 3 ether, making settlement revert on insufficient balance in cases where the original would succeed.
Move the guess reset (guesses[msg.sender].block = 0) from before the hash comparison to inside the winning branch after the external transfer, so losing guesses remain locked.
